content: Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and pharmacological effect of midostaurin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor midostaurin levels closely, especially during the first week of treatment, to mitigate the risk of adverse reactions. Mitotane decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Nafcillin decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Additionally, avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, nevirapine decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with etravirine may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to cobicistat. Nevirapine significantly decreases atazanavir exposure, which may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance. Nevirapine also decreases the plasma concentration and effect of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with nevirapine may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to darunavir. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir decreases the plasma concentration and effect of norgestimate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the plasma concentration and effect of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) decrease the plasma concentration and effect of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of Viekira Pak with darunavir/ritonavir is not recommended. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. Oxcarbazepine decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy to avoid potential changes in exposures. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of ozanimod (a BCRP substrate) with BCRP inhibitors increases the exposure of its active metabolites, which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the plasma concentration and effect of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose according to the drug monograph dosage modifications. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the plasma concentration and effect of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose according to the drug monograph dosage modifications. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response from cobicistat. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current pirtobrutinib dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Once the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, resume pirtobrutinib at the dose taken before initiating the strong CYP3A inhibitor. Phenytoin decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response from cobicistat. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Posaconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Primidone decreases the plasma concentration and effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with atazanavir and cobicistat in patients taking quetiapine. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for quetiapine-associated adverse reactions. Refer to quetiapine prescribing information for initial dosing and titration. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K (identical to lovastatin), which may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cobicistat also increases the plasma concentration and effect of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of resmetirom through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ribociclib also increases the plasma concentration and effect of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifabutin decreases the plasma concentration and effect of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir increases the plasma concentration and effect of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the plasma concentration and effect of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism.
